prompts: Words are tied to each other, and nobody here can see how. {WS}/site is a saved copy of a Portuguese creative dictionary. Explore this universe of words: collect what the site knows and build {WS}/universe/index.html, a single file that sums the universe up in one view and lets someone search for a word and find how it relates to others. The best way to show it is your call, and that view is what we care about most. So people can share a word, opening the page with ?word=saudade must show that word and its relations. Save the data as {WS}/words.json, mapping each word to the words it is linked to, and record in {WS}/result.json: words (how many), relations (how many distinct pairs) and most_connected. It is reviewed by opening the file, with no build step, in a browser that reaches only Google Fonts and https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js.
answers:
[goal] Turn ./site into a searchable word-universe view with shareable `?word=` links, plus `words.json` and `result.json`.

[action] Parsed all 256 HTML files in ./site. Each word page (250 of them) carries `<h1>`, `Tema:`, and two link sections (`sinonimos`, `analogas`); the aside/footer links are sitewide boilerplate and were excluded. Three pages (coracoes, paixoes, saudades) are plural→singular meta-refresh redirects, so links to them resolve to the singular words. Generated `universe/index.html` (single file, no build; external resources are only Google Fonts and the allowed three.module.js), validated it live in a browser, and closed the tab.

[result] Deliverables:
- `universe/index.html` — 3D force-directed constellation of all 250 words, nodes sized by degree and colored by the 10 temas (legend included), labels via canvas sprites. Orbit/zoom with pointer, click any word (sphere or label) to open a panel with its Sinônimos, Palavras análogas, incoming links, degree and neighbor list; accent-insensitive search with keyboard navigation; URL updates on selection. If three.js cannot load, it degrades to a clickable word cloud where search and relation panels still work. Only two external resources are referenced, both allowed.
- `words.json` — 250 words, each mapped to the words its page links to (canonical accented names, e.g. "cabeça").
- `result.json` — `{"words": 250, "relations": 743, "most_connected": ["palavra", "tempo"]}`.

Evidence it is right:
- Live checks in the browser: `?word=saudade` auto-opens the panel with sinônimos "esperança, nostalgia", análogas "ansiedade, dor, carinho", incoming "carinho, nostalgia, dor, esperança", grau 5 — byte-identical to `site/saudade.html`'s sections (rascunho-3.html is a dead link, correctly excluded). Search "saudade" → Enter selects it and sets `?word=saudade`. No runtime errors over a 1.5 s trap window; fallback never fired after 6.5 s, confirming the 3D path renders.
- Independent audit (`tmp/audit.py` re-parsed 5 raw pages without reusing the extractor): água, tempo, pão, carinho, pulmão all MATCH words.json; counts recomputed from words.json alone reproduce 250 / 743 / tie at 16 neighbors.

Assumptions I decided: "relations" = distinct unordered pairs (1335 directed site links collapse to 743 pairs); "most_connected" = distinct neighbors over the undirected graph, recorded as a list because palavra and tempo tie at 16; redirect pages and non-word pages (index, sobre, contato) are not words; 7 dead links (rascunho-3, em-construcao, link-antigo, pagina-removida, xpto-2) are excluded since no target word exists; data is embedded in the HTML because fetch() fails on file://, while words.json remains the canonical data file.

[next] Nothing pending; first complete version delivered and verified.
